relatedSnapshot.title: Whop blocks payment-plan checkout for buyers who already own the product — handle automatically
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What is wrong

Reps take a deposit (one-time payment on a Whop product), then send the customer an Acquisity "Payment plan" link for the remaining balance on the same product. Whop rejects the checkout with "This product is not available through this checkout. Please contact the seller."

Whop's rule: a buyer who already holds a membership on a product cannot check out a plan that carries `trial_period_days`. Every Acquisity split-pay/subscription link sends `trial_period_days` — it is how "first recurring payment in N days / $0 due today" is implemented (`getFirstRenewalDelayDays` in `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/checkout-schedule.ts`, sent in `providers/whop/checkout.ts` since #6289). So any returning buyer is blocked. Removing the trial is not an option — it is what delays the first charge.

Confirmed in prod: `<email>` already had a Whop membership on `<stripe-id>` (AIA Name 1) from her $7,500 deposit; every later payment-plan link fails at checkout. Links still work for first-time buyers.

## What is wanted

Make this flow work automatically — the rep should not have to know about Whop's rule or fix it in the Whop dashboard. Options to evaluate:

* Detect (via Whop API or stored member data) that the buyer/contact already has a membership on the selected product, and warn or block in the payment link builder before the link is sent.
* Auto-route the installment plan to a separate "installments/payment plan" Whop product for that company so the repurchase check never fires.
* Or reuse the existing Whop membership (attach/change plan server-side via the Whop API) instead of a new checkout.

Whop's own guidance for this error: send a pricing option without a trial, or use a different pass/product.

## Done when

* A rep can send a payment-plan link to a customer who already paid a deposit on the same product, and checkout succeeds (or the builder prevents the dead link with a clear reason up front).
* No new link can be created in a state Whop will always reject.

## Context

Slack thread: <url:acquisityworkspace.slack.com>
Failed links: <url:app.acquisity.ai> and <url:app.acquisity.ai> (AIA Name 1 org)

relatedSnapshot.title: When payment gives up, stop the plan, mailboxes and domains cleanly
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

ENG-8112 documented the original seven-day warning and auto-cancel decision. The operating model was revised on 11 September 2026 after measuring how billing actually works. Inboxes are charged monthly on each subscription's own anniversary and domains yearly, so there is no advance invoice 28 or 14 days before renewal. When a payment fails we warn the customer, let the provider's retries run, then switch provider renewal off so the inboxes expire at the end of the month we have already paid for, leaving a free reactivation window. This ticket owns production enforcement across payment events, base-plan/workspace termination, Zapmail, Company One, local state, recovery and audit evidence.

**Scope narrowed 29 Sep 2026.** This ticket now owns Flow B (the plan ends because the customer did not pay), Flow C (a mailbox payment fails while the plan is fine), the reactivation window and the provider-neutral design. Three parts moved out:

* the cancel steps themselves (renewal off at the supplier, per-domain resumable billing cancel) now live in ENG-14252;
* workspace and account deletion now lives in ENG-10782;
* the Autumn event classifier, the failure reason and the day 0, 3 and 7 warnings now live in ENG-13746.

Added: on Autumn, an expired plan never pauses campaigns today, because Autumn workspaces are always treated as protected. Autumn plans that expire must run the same pause and cleanup as Whop, and the automation switch (`SUBSCRIPTION_ACCESS_AUTOMATION_ENABLED`) is turned on after a dry-run review. Whether Acquisity/Acquisity#6288 is finished here or closed is an open question; recommended: close it and reuse the parts this ticket needs.

**Decided 29 Sep 2026:** no immediate cut-off. When billing stops (day 14, Stripe's final retry), supplier renewal is switched off and the mailboxes keep working until the month we have already paid the supplier for ends, then they are removed. We never cancel at the supplier early. The full timeline is on ENG-13358.

## Problem in plain English

When a mailbox payment fails, a base workspace plan is cancelled, or a workspace is deleted, customer access and Zapmail supplier billing can drift apart. Acquisity may stop collecting mailbox revenue while the Zapmail domain subscription remains live and billable.

A deletion can also remove the local records needed to find the supplier subscription later. One failed step can leave the mailbox active in Zapmail, connected in Company One, hidden locally, or some combination of those states.

## Confirmed production gap

The production Autumn webhook transport is configured and receiving signed events, but the current handler only acts on new, renew, upgrade and downgrade base-plan transitions. It accepts `past_due`, `expired` and `cancel` events with HTTP 200, marks them processed and performs no mailbox cancellation or reconciliation. Since 11 August, 947 `past_due` events for domain or inbox products across 113 billing accounts reached this path without triggering supplier cleanup.

This ticket must change that behavior. Relevant events must be classified and durably enqueued. They must not be acknowledged as successfully processed when the required state transition was skipped.

## Detailed behavior

### How renewal timing actually works (measured 11 September 2026)

* Each inbox subscription renews monthly on its own anniversary. The provider charges us about a day before it, and the customer's Autumn anniversary is effectively the same moment (median gap under an hour across a 1,800 domain sample).
* So a failed customer payment has always already cost us one provider month. Accept that month rather than moving billing anchors.
* About 12% of pre-warmed domains were registered as provider stock before a customer bought them, so their provider dates differ from the customer's. Every cutoff must use the provider period end, never the customer billing date.
* Domains are yearly and renew separately. Domain renewal is owned by ENG-13745.

### What cancel means (the same steps for every reason)

1. **Stop charging.** For a customer's own cancellation, stop at the end of the period they have paid for. For non-payment, stop immediately with no further retries.
2. **Switch provider renewal off for the inbox subscription.** The inboxes keep working until the end of the month already paid for, then expire. Never cancel immediately while a paid month is running.
3. **Reactivation window.** Until that provider month ends, a customer who pays or resubscribes gets everything back: renewal back on, billing re-attached, inboxes still warm.
4. **At the end of the provider month,** once the provider confirms the inboxes expired: remove them from sending (where sending is a separate provider), mark the domain and inboxes cancelled, email the customer, and switch domain renewal off so the domain is not renewed.
5. **Campaigns pause when the plan ends,** not when the inboxes expire. This is ENG-10751 behaviour extended to Autumn.

### Flow B: the plan ends because the customer did not pay

Day 0 is the failed payment.

* Days 0 to about 14: the warnings in ENG-13746 while Autumn retries the card.
* About day 14: the plan expires. Plan, inboxes and domains all cancel using the steps above and campaigns pause. Email: "Your plan has ended. Your inboxes will be removed on {provider month end} unless you reactivate."
* 3 days before removal: "Last chance to keep your inboxes."
* At removal: "Your inboxes and domains were removed."
* Payment recovered at any point before removal: everything is restored and the customer gets "Payment received, you're all set."

### Flow C: an inbox payment fails while the plan is fine

* The same as Flow B but scoped to that domain's inboxes.
* Day 0: alert and email, "Payment failed for 12 inboxes on <domain>", with the failure reason and how to fix it. Reminders on day 3 and day 7, and a final warning 2 days before the stop date, each repeating the reason (decided 29 Sep 2026).
* At Autumn expiry: stop billing and switch provider renewal off. Take those inboxes out of active campaigns so campaigns keep sending from the rest.
* Reactivation window until the provider month ends, then removal and an email.

### Works with any inbox provider

We plan to move inboxes to Company One. The timeline, reactivation window, emails and campaign pause live on our side, keyed to a generic provider period end. Each provider adapter supplies: read an inbox subscription's period end and renewal state; switch renewal on or off; renew or restore; confirm the inboxes ended; remove them from sending; list all inventory for the daily check. Where the provider and the sending platform are the same company, the remove-from-sending step is a no-op. Confirm how Company One bills us before writing that adapter.

### Also fix

A customer cancelling a single domain goes through the same steps, ending at the end of the paid period on both sides. Today the provider is cancelled immediately while Autumn bills to period end, so the customer loses service they have paid for.

### Durable renewal and cancellation workflow

Use an explicit resumable paid lifecycle:

`notice_scheduled → customer_charge_due → paid_for_next_period → supplier_renewal_due → supplier_renewal_verified → occurrence_completed → next_occurrence_scheduled`

After failed collection:

`cure_window → supplier_nonrenewal_requested → supplier_nonrenewal_verified → supplier_period_ended → full_domain_deletion_requested → full_domain_deleted → downstream_cleanup_pending → billing_reconciled → completed`

Each transition records attempts, timestamp, idempotency key, provider response summary and last error. A retry resumes at the first incomplete transition and cannot repeat completed external actions.

For a managed inbox domain, an inbox subscription still unpaid at the safe cutoff schedules supplier non-renewal while preserving the already-paid mailbox period. Only after that period ends and conclusive provider readback confirms service ended may Acquisity delete the full associated domain and every included inbox. Customer notices must explicitly explain this whole-domain consequence.

Terminal Zapmail deletion uses Cold Mail Reseller `DELETE /domains`, which deprovisions the domain, DNS, mailboxes and associated subscriptions. Provider contract correction, verified 9 September 2026: the CMR subscription event contract says the cancel endpoint takes effect immediately and deactivates mailbox accounts. It must not be treated as end-of-cycle nonrenewal or dispatched early while promising the funded period remains available. Disabling subscription auto-renew is a separate, documented operation (`POST /subscriptions/toggle-autorenewal`). Per the provider's documented lifecycle, renewal off means the subscription goes past due at period end, gets a 7 day grace period, then expires and the mailboxes are deactivated. Verify this once in the provider sandbox, including that the paid month keeps running and that switching renewal back on restores the mailboxes, before wiring the production flow. An accepted cancellation request is not proof of full-domain cleanup.

Before completing cancellation, calculate any remaining customer-funded annual-domain value and record the explicitly approved refund, credit or no-refund outcome on the renewal occurrence. Existing historical waste handled by ENG-13362 may still require immediate full-domain deletion after fresh evidence and explicit approval.

Supplier deletion is confirmed only by the required response and conclusive domain/subscription readback. Company One and local cleanup run only after the current supplier period ended and readback confirms service ended or the domain was deleted. A future non-renewal alone is not cleanup authorization. Downstream failures remain independently retryable and cannot restart supplier service, block cost prevention or repeat a destructive action.

### Workspace and account deletion

* Workspace, billing-account, order and mailbox deletion must not cascade away supplier identity or cancellation evidence.
* Trigger the same deprovisioning workflow before destructive deletion, or retain a tombstone until cleanup is complete.
* If safety requires blocking deletion until supplier cleanup succeeds, return a clear operator/customer error.
* Cover self-service, admin, bulk, script and framework deletion entry points that can affect the scoped inventory.

### Recovery, reversals and billing access

* Payment recovery before supplier non-renewal returns the occurrence to `paid_for_next_period`.
* Recovery after non-renewal was requested requires authoritative provider reconciliation. If cancellation cannot be reversed, either provision a new explicitly approved resource or refund/credit the customer; never claim the old resource was restored.
* Recovery after provider deletion requires new checkout or approved comp and never silently recreates infrastructure.
* A refund, dispute, chargeback or credit reversal before the supplier cutoff makes the future period uncovered and enters the cure/non-renewal path.
* If money is reversed after Acquisity paid the supplier, preserve live service for the funded supplier period, flag the contradiction, prevent the next renewal and apply the approved debt/refund/access policy.
* If the customer cancels after advance collection, refund only when supplier renewal can still be safely prevented. Otherwise preserve service for the funded period and schedule the following renewal off.
* If the customer paid but supplier renewal fails, enter supplier recovery and preserve entitlement plus Company One/local linkage. Complete only after readback proves restored service, or apply the defined refund/credit outcome if it cannot be restored.
* Ending the base workspace plan does not itself prove a separately paid or approved-free inbox subscription is unpaid. Evaluate each managed inbox domain against its own inbox entitlement and supplier period.
* Customers without an active base plan retain a billing-only route to view affected resources, warning, amount, payment recovery and cancellation deadline.

## Suggested implementation route

* Extend the signed Autumn event path and scheduled renewal backstop around the same durable renewal occurrence. Name 2 advance payment failure and recovery quickly; scheduled jobs own the reminder steps, the cutoff at the provider period end and the final provider readback. Provider calls stay outside the webhook request.
* Keep provider calls out of the webhook request. Persist the event idempotently, enqueue the durable workflow, and return success only after the required transition has been recorded.
* Route delinquency deadlines, base-plan termination and workspace deletion through one shared cancellation orchestrator.
* Build the state machine on durable records introduced by the entitlement ticket.
* Derive idempotency from the immutable entitlement plus cancellation occurrence, not from a domain name or scheduler run.
* Reuse the existing Cold Mail Reseller cancellation audit foundation where it satisfies these guarantees.
* Add operational alerts and an admin view for incomplete or repeatedly failing transitions.

## Done when

* the existing Autumn webhook no longer acknowledges and discards relevant `past_due`, `expired` or `cancel` events;
* tests prove the exact event scenarios above enqueue one idempotent transition and irrelevant products remain ignored;
* every cutoff is derived from the provider period end, and duplicate events cannot reset a deadline or the notification history;
* duplicate events cannot reset grace or duplicate cancellation;
* payment recovery before supplier cancellation stops pending removal;
* supplier, Company One, local and billing steps are resumable and individually auditable;
* base-plan cancellation and every workspace deletion path trigger the same guarantees;
* deletion cannot erase the evidence needed to finish cleanup;
* full-domain supplier deletion is verified against the exact domain, supplier subscription and included mailbox quantity;
* `/subscriptions/cancel` cannot be mistaken for completed full-domain offboarding;
* active campaigns are recorded and paused before Company One removal, while Company One or local failure cannot block or repeat confirmed Zapmail deletion;
* incomplete workflows alert with the failed transition, age and estimated monthly supplier cost;
* integration tests cover payment recovery before and after supplier cancellation, duplicate events, partial provider failure, workspace deletion with active mailboxes and retry from every transition.
* customer notices identify the full affected domain/inboxes, amount, charge date, cutoff and whole-domain deletion consequence;
* provider non-renewal preserves the already-paid period and never authorizes early Company One/local disconnection;
* an unpaid managed inbox-domain subscription can delete the full domain only after period-end readback and deterministic annual-domain refund/credit/no-refund handling;
* deadlines are derived from authoritative supplier timestamps and stored in UTC; missing or drifting dates become operator exceptions;
* changed quantity, price or renewal timestamp invalidates the stale occurrence before collection;
* paid customer/supplier renewal failure enters recovery and ends only in verified restored service or deterministic refund/credit;
* tests cover payment recovery racing the cutoff, duplicate scheduler/webhook delivery, provider timeout after non-renewal, and two workers claiming the same occurrence;
* the base-plan cascade runs: plan expiry cancels inboxes and domains through the same steps, and campaigns pause at plan expiry;
* Flow C removes only the unpaid domain's inboxes while other campaigns keep sending;
* paying inside the reactivation window restores everything with no new setup or provisioning;
* no provider inbox stays live with renewal on for a customer who is not paying, checked by the daily read.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14252, for the shared cancel steps.
* ENG-13746, for the event classifier and warnings.

Do not run this at the same time as ENG-11454: both add a "stop at plan end" step, and whichever lands second reuses the first.

## Implementation context

AI context.md

### Existing-inbox management implementation slice (9 September 2026)

After ENG-13526, James confirmed that Acquisity/Acquisity#6288 must provide one owner/admin link to see all existing inbox groups, including active paid, free and credit-funded groups, with actual customer prices and current service periods. Clients can keep all, cancel all, or keep some whole domain groups and cancel others. Choices and their consequences must be reviewed before confirmation.

Keeping a group must recover any exact existing invoice without duplicating it, repair future payment collection where needed, and establish or restore recurring billing for retained inboxes without purchasing or provisioning new ones. Paying an invoice alone is not completion. Show invoice liabilities separately from future monthly charges. Preserve paid siblings, allocate shared coverage once, and keep annual domain/platform rights separate. Cancellation must record and verify exact billing and supplier effects, preserve funded periods, and show requested, scheduled, pending and completed states honestly. Promises, internal budgets and reversals require their recorded decisions before any automatic demand.

This scope supersedes the earlier invoice-only and selection-only implementation limitation. It retains this ticket's existing ownership and broader lifecycle contract, and reuses ENG-13359 entitlement and ENG-13361 reconciliation work. Unsupported or ambiguous provider actions must have a specific guided resolution and must not be reported as completed.

Implementation, tests and the draft PR are authorized, including a dedicated access-protected preview using a separate synthetic database and Autumn/Stripe test credentials. Production issuance, notices, real charges/refunds, production subscription changes, supplier cancellations, rollout and merge are not authorized. Outreach sending remains dependent on a verified working flow. This slice does not mark the lifecycle programme or estate cleanup complete.

relatedSnapshot.description:
## Issue Identified:

When users who do not yet have their AI SDR + CEA activated press the new **Start Onboarding** button from the "Complete the new onboarding.." banner, they are directed to payment page they cannot escape.

## Steps to Reproduce:

* User does not yet have the AI SDR + CEA activated
* User sees the banner "Complete the new onboarding for a better experience" and presses the Start Onboarding button

 <image> 

* User is taken to the "Set up your account" page, and is shown a payment modal 

 <image> 

* User is unable to escape this screen

## Expected Behavior:

A user should have a way to back out of this process, if they are taken to the "Set up your account' page and aren't ready to pay.

**IMPORTANT**: This issue is also affecting internal AIA Admins, who are not paying customers but need to access the production instance for customer support tasks.

* Name 6 is not able to access production currently because of this issue

## Name 4:

* Name: Name 5
* Email: <email>

---

Some QA-based context from <mention>:

I think it may be an issue for basic plan / no plan organizations only

Why?
We have a payment gate in onboarding that applies to organization onboarding flow.
Only completely new accounts have payment gate later, on CEA and SDR

So I would guess that restarting onboarding before having any payment gets locked on payment gate

And the only onboarding scenario for which we allow exiting onboarding is for new organizations under existing accounts

\--

Update after tests on staging:

Everything worked for me on plan types:

* legacy
* legacy pro
* pro

I was able to reproduce for Basic plan and this issue is NOT related to the new banner. The new banner only triggers onboarding. I intentionally restarted onboarding from settings and got the issue from above. Recording:

<url:jam.dev>

\--

Potential fix: just disable payment gate for organization's onboarding_status "reset"

relatedSnapshot.title: main is broken by PR #6430: manual payment recording fails typecheck and blocks pushes
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

`bun typecheck` fails on main because manual payment recording reads a value that can now be empty without checking it first. Until it is fixed, every branch that merges main fails its pre-push typecheck in a file the author never touched.

## Problem

Two payment changes that merged today do not fit together. Acquisity/Acquisity#6444 made the step that marks a payment as successful return nothing when the payment was already recorded as successful. Acquisity/Acquisity#6430 then added code in `recordManualPayment` that reads the payment trigger from that result without checking whether it exists. Typecheck reports `'successfulPaymentResult' is possibly 'null'` at `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/services/manual-payments.ts(859,11)`. Anyone branching from or merging main is blocked from pushing.

## Proposed fix

Check the result of the payment success step right after it runs, and fail the whole payment if it comes back empty instead of carrying on. A freshly recorded manual payment can never legitimately get an empty result, so if it ever does, the payment rolls back rather than committing without its deal recalculation, auto-win and activity. No payment behavior changes on any reachable path.

## What's included

* An explicit check in `recordManualPayment`, right after the payment success step, that throws if the result is empty, and reading the trigger directly afterwards.
* Confirming `bun typecheck` and the existing manual payment tests pass afterward.
* Not included: any change to how a payment is marked successful, the repair flow from PR fix(crm): correct Whop payment sync and add reviewed repairs, or the public API from PR feat(api): public API scopes and routes for manual payments (ENG-13936). Neither PR is reverted or reworked.

## How it should work

Recording a manual payment from the Record payment button, the public API or a workflow behaves exactly as before. The pending trigger is still saved in the same transaction as the money, so a crash before delivery stays recoverable. If the payment success step ever returns nothing for a payment that was just created, the whole transaction fails and rolls back, so no payment is left committed without its side effects.

## Who can do what

Not applicable: internal build-health fix with no permission or role changes.

## What the user sees

Not applicable: no visible change. Engineers get a compiling main again.

## Done when

* `bun typecheck` from the repo root passes with no error in `manual-payments.ts`.
* The existing manual payment tests still pass, including the database suite `manual-payments-db.test.ts` and the public API handler test.
* Recording a manual payment still stores its pending trigger and delivers exactly one payment event.
* An empty result from the payment success step fails the transaction instead of committing the payment.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Main compiles again and engineers can merge it into their branches and push.

## Implementation context

* Cause: fix(crm): correct Whop payment sync and add reviewed repairs (merged 2026-09-18 10:47 UTC) added two paths in `applySuccessfulPaymentInTransaction` that return `null`: a `payment_succeeded` event already exists for the payment, or a processed repair already recorded its success. feat(api): public API scopes and routes for manual payments (ENG-13936) (merged 2026-09-18 17:25 UTC) reads `.successfulPaymentTrigger` at `manual-payments.ts:859` with no null check, while line 877 in the same function already uses `?.`. Line numbers are as of main at `eddc96e508`.
* Name 11 risk: none. A manual payment row is inserted moments earlier in the same transaction with a fresh id, so no earlier success event can exist, and it has no provider payment or connection id, so no repair can match. The null cannot occur on this path, so this is a type-only break.
* Chosen approach: throw right after the call when the result is `null`, then read `successfulPaymentResult.successfulPaymentTrigger` directly at both places. Changed after review: the first version skipped the pending trigger when the result was empty, but an empty result comes back before the contract recalculation, auto-win and payment activity run, so that version would have let the payment commit without them.
* Related: ENG-13936 (the manual payments API work that PR feat(api): public API scopes and routes for manual payments (ENG-13936) belongs to, still in progress) and ENG-13403 (the Whop payment sync work behind PR fix(crm): correct Whop payment sync and add reviewed repairs, done). Neither is changed by this ticket.
* First reported in the engineering Slack thread.

relatedSnapshot.title: Let closers choose which payment methods a buyer sees on a CRM payment link
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Closers create payment links in the CRM to collect money from customers. Today every link shows the same set of payment options at checkout. Closers have asked to control which options a specific customer sees. There is no way to do that anywhere in the product right now.

This ticket adds a "Payment methods" control to the payment link builder.

## Background for anyone new to this area

* CRM payments run through **Whop**, a third-party payments platform. Each customer organisation connects their own Whop account (stored in `crm_payment_provider_connection`).
* When a closer creates a payment link, our code creates a hidden **plan** in Whop plus a checkout configuration, and gets back a purchase URL. The buyer lands on our wrapper page at `/pay/[publicToken]`, which embeds Whop's checkout in an iframe.
* **Whop decides which payment methods appear**, filtered by the amount, the buyer's country, and the seller's account settings. We currently send no preference at all.
* Alongside card and bank transfer, Whop offers financing providers (ClarityPay, Name 13, Name 14, Name 15, Name 16, Zip). Each has its own maximum amount, e.g. ClarityPay caps at $30,000 and Zip at $1,500. Above a provider's cap it simply does not appear.

## Problem

A closer cannot turn a payment method off for a link. Feedback came via Name 12 on 2026-08-01: closers "mentioned not being able to toggle certain payment methods on/off when creating payment links".

## Solution

Whop's API accepts a `payment_method_configuration` object, shaped:

```
{ enabled: string[], disabled: string[], include_platform_defaults: boolean }
```

Pass a per-link selection through to it.

**Critical placement detail:** this must be set on the **plan** object, not at the checkout-configuration top level. Whop's SDK states the top-level field "currently only works in 'setup' mode", and our flow uses `mode: 'payment'`. Setting it in the wrong place fails silently with no error.

To hide a method while keeping everything else, send `include_platform_defaults: true` with the method in `disabled`.

## Scope

**1. Storage**

* New `jsonb` column on `crm_payment_link_version` holding Whop's exact shape. It goes on the *version*, not the link, because `updateUnpaidLink` creates a new version and re-creates the Whop plan each time, and the version already stores `provider_request_payload`.

**2. Pass-through**

* `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/providers/whop/checkout.ts` → `buildPlanPayload()`. Both the one-time and the renewal branches.
* Thread through `CreateWhopCheckoutForCrmLinkParams` → `createProviderCheckout` → `createCrmPaymentLink` and `updateUnpaidLink`, plus the `createLink` and `updateUnpaidLink` tRPC inputs in `apps/web/trpc/routers/crm/payments.ts`.
* **Must be strictly additive.** When no selection is stored, send no `payment_method_configuration` at all so existing behaviour is byte-identical.

**3. Builder UI**

All UI work is in `apps/web/components/crm/payments/payment-link-builder.tsx`.

### Design reference

**Interactive mockup: <url>

Open it and click through it. It is a working React component, not a static image: change the amount, switch payment type, flip the toggles, and the behaviour below is all demonstrated live. Build to match it.

The mockup reproduces the current page layout (header, product grid, template picker, payment type, amount, advanced options, buyer preview, sticky footer) so the diff against today's page is easy to see.

**Design signed off by James on 2026-08-04.** Three decisions were explicitly settled and should not be reopened without asking him:

* Unavailable methods **grey out and stay visible**, they do not hide. The closer should learn why an option is not offered.
* The amount-limit chips (`Up to $30,000`) **stay**. They tell a closer which rails a deal size can actually use.
* **Recurring stays** in the payment type options.

### New: Payment methods control

Goes in **Advanced options**, as the **first** row. Use the existing two-column row layout (label plus description on the left, control on the right) that Currency and Expiration days already use.

One row per payment method. Each row has:

* A small coloured dot for the provider.
* The provider name.
* A status chip, following these rules in order:
  * If the method is card or bank transfer, show `Always on`.
  * If it is unavailable because of the payment type, show `Not available on payment plans`.
  * If it is unavailable because the link amount exceeds its cap, show `Over their $X limit`.
  * Otherwise, if the method has a cap, show `Up to $X`.
* A one-line plain-English description (see wording below).
* A toggle on the right.

Unavailable rows get a `#fafbfc` background, greyed text, a faded dot, and a disabled toggle. They stay visible rather than disappearing, so the closer learns why an option is not offered.

Below the list: "Greyed out options cannot go on this link. Either the amount is over their limit, they do not work with this payment type, or they are not available in this currency."

When the payment type is Recurring or Payment plan, show an amber callout above the list:

> Financing is off because you picked a payment plan. If the buyer wants to pay monthly, choose **Pay in full** instead. ClarityPay spreads it over 36 months and we still get paid in full today.

### Method list, order, caps and copy

| Method | Cap | Default | Description |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Card | none | Always on, locked | Visa, Mastercard, Name 17. Charged in full today. |
| Bank transfer | none | Always on, locked | ACH or wire. No card fees, takes a few days to land. |
| ClarityPay | $30,000 | On | Buyer pays monthly for up to 36 months. We get paid in full today. |
| Name 13 | $20,000 | On | Splits across credit the buyer already has. No credit check. |
| Name 14 | $10,000 | Off | Name 18 over up to 24 months. |
| Name 15 | $4,000 | Off | Four instalments over six weeks. |
| Name 16 | $2,500 | Off | Pay in 2, pay in 4, or monthly. |
| Zip | $1,500 | Off | Four instalments over six weeks. |
| Name 19 | none | Off | Name 20 and other coins. One-time USD links only. |

Caps come from Whop's published limits (docs.whop.com/payments-and-billing/financing/all-bnpl-options) and match LT's actual payment history. Everything except card, bank transfer and crypto counts as financing for the payment-type rule. Name 19 is not financing, but Whop documents it as one-time USD only, so it is also unavailable on recurring and payment-plan links.

### Buyer preview must show the selected methods

The right-hand "Buyer preview" panel currently renders a hardcoded "Card details" field. Replace it with a live list of the methods that are actually enabled, first one selected. This is the point of the feature: the closer needs to see what the buyer will see.

## Copy fixes (same PR)

All agreed and shown in the mockup.

| Where | Now | Change to |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Product cards | `Onetime payment · US$0-US$1,000,000` | `Pay in full · Usually $995` where the product has a dominant price, `Pay in full · Price varies` where it does not |
| Payment type buttons | Bare labels with no explanation | Add a one-line description under each (see below) |
| Amount section | `Customize the amount for this deal.` heading plus a second `How much are you charging?` label | One label: `How much are you charging for this deal?` |
| Expiration days | `Expiration days` / `Optional number of days before the link expires.` | `Link expires after` / `Leave blank and the link never expires.` with a `days` suffix inside the field |
| Sticky footer | `Buyer will pay US$1,000 USD once` | `Buyer will pay US$1,000 once` (US$ already carries the currency) |
| Currency | `Locked to the selected deal currency.` | `Currency is determined by the product you pick.` and moved to the bottom of Advanced options |

Payment type descriptions:

* **Pay in full** — One charge. They can still spread it out with a financing option.
* **Recurring** — Charges again every period until cancelled. Card or bank only.
* **Payment plan** — We collect the instalments ourselves. Card or bank only.

**Note on the product card price.** `US$0-US$1,000,000` is the internal min/max guard from `crm_payment_product_config`, identical on all 17 LT products, and tells a closer nothing. Showing a usual price needs a new aggregate over succeeded payments per product. If that is more than you want in this PR, just drop the range and show the payment type alone. Do not ship the guard range as-is.

## Name 21 the UI must handle

* **Card and bank transfer are always on** and cannot be switched off. Every link needs at least one non-financing route.
* Financing providers and one-time-only methods do not work on payment plans or recurring links. Verified against every payment in production: only card and bank transfer have ever backed a recurring charge. All financing appears exclusively as one-off, and Whop documents Name 19 as one-time USD only. So when the closer picks "Payment plan" or "Recurring", financing options and Name 19 must be disabled with an explanation.
* **A provider whose cap is below the link amount cannot be offered.** Disable it and say why, rather than letting the closer think they have offered it.

## Also in this ticket: fix the Currency field

Two connected problems, folded in here because they live in the same Advanced options panel.

**The label is wrong.** The Currency field is disabled and described as "Locked to the selected deal currency." That is not what it does. `apps/web/components/crm/payments/payment-link-builder.tsx` line 1011:

```
const currency = selectedProduct?.config?.currency ?? 'usd';
```

It follows the **product's** currency, never the deal's. The product's currency is inherited from the synced Whop plan when the product is first enabled (`apps/web/trpc/routers/crm/payments.ts` around line 1185: `defaultPlan?.currency ?? firstPlan?.currency ?? 'usd'`) and there is no way to change it anywhere in the UI. So the field tells the user it follows the deal, while actually following the product, and offering no way to influence either.

**A non-USD deal cannot get a payment link at all.** `assertDealCanAcceptCurrency` in `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/services/payment-links.ts` line 129 throws when the deal's currency differs from the product's:

```
if (deal.currency && deal.currency.toLowerCase() !== params.currency) {
  throw new Error('Deal already uses a different currency');
}
```

What a closer experiences:

1. They create a deal in EUR.
2. They open the builder and pick a product. 16 of the 17 enabled LT products are configured in USD.
3. Currency shows USD, greyed out, with no way to change it.
4. Create link fails with "Deal already uses a different currency".

There is no path forward from that screen. The only working combination is the single EUR-configured product.

Blast radius today is small: LT has 15,874 USD deals and exactly 1 non-USD deal. Nobody has hit it in the wild. It becomes live the moment a closer sets a deal to anything other than USD.

**This is not about supporting multiple currencies.** LT confirmed on 2026-08-03 that everything stays USD. Non-US buyers can still pay; their own bank converts at its rate. That is deliberate: `adaptive_pricing_enabled: false` is set on every plan we create (`apps/web/lib/whop/plan-fields.ts`, from PR #5125) and `?currency=usd` is forced onto the checkout URL (`apps/web/lib/whop/checkout-url.ts`).

What to do:

1. Replace the label copy with **"Currency is determined by the product you pick."**
2. Move the Currency row to the **bottom** of Advanced options. It is the least actionable field there.
3. Stop the dead end. Either prevent the mismatch being reachable (validate at product selection and explain inline), or make the error tell the closer what to change. "Deal already uses a different currency" gives them nothing.

Additional acceptance criteria:

* The Currency field no longer claims to follow the deal.
* Currency is the last row in Advanced options.
* A closer with a non-USD deal either cannot reach the failure, or is told plainly what to change.
* No change to which currency is actually charged. Everything stays USD.

## Out of scope

* Org-level or per-product defaults. Per-link only for now.
* Multi-currency support. Everything stays USD.
* Role-based permissions (e.g. a method only team leads can enable). Flagged as a possible future ask, deliberately not built here.

## Acceptance criteria

* A closer can turn individual payment methods off when creating a payment link.
* The selection reaches Whop and the buyer sees only the remaining methods at checkout.
* A link created without touching the control behaves exactly as it does today.
* Card and bank transfer cannot be switched off.
* Financing options and one-time-only methods such as Name 19 are unavailable on payment plan and recurring links, with a visible reason.
* Options above their amount cap are unavailable, with a visible reason.
* Editing an unpaid link preserves the selection onto the new version.

## Risk

Production-critical. Every LT closer is creating payment links this week. Changes touch live payment code, so the pass-through must default to today's exact behaviour when nothing is configured.

relatedSnapshot.title: Recover failed Whop payments from CRM with safe retry actions
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Let permitted CRM users help a customer recover a failed Whop payment by retrying an eligible charge or opening Whop's recovery flow.

**Deferred: keep this ticket in Backlog. Payment visibility and accurate statuses are being delivered first. Do not implement or enable these actions yet.**

## Problem

Once a rep understands why a payment failed, there is no supported recovery action in the inspected CRM payment UI. Whop provides a retry API and recovery information, but using them can initiate a new charge and needs separate permissions and testing.

## User experience

From a failed payment's details, an authorized user can see which recovery options Whop currently allows. Before retrying a charge, show the customer, amount and payment method and require confirmation. If Whop supplies a recovery URL, allow the permitted user to open that flow. Show the resulting processing, success or failure state in the payment history.

## What's included

* Retry an existing payment only when Whop currently confirms it is eligible.
* Open Whop's provider-supplied recovery flow when available.
* Clear unavailable, processing, failed and completed states.
* An audit entry recording who requested recovery, when and the result.
* Reuse payment visibility and accurate statuses for the result and transaction history.
* No automatic retries, recovery emails/messages, new payment links, refund/void/capture controls or subscription changes.

## How it should work

Recheck permission, workspace ownership and current provider state on the server before requesting a charge. Prevent double-clicks and concurrent requests from charging twice. If the provider response is uncertain, reconcile the result before allowing another retry. Opening a recovery flow alone must not mark the payment successful.

## Who can do what

The permission policy must be settled before implementation. Recommended default: owner/admin only for charge retries, with any closer access explicitly granted through the existing CRM permission system. Viewing a payment does not grant permission to charge it.

## Done when

* An eligible failed payment can be recovered through the supported Whop action by an authorized user.
* Ineligible payments and unauthorized or wrong-workspace requests are blocked on the server.
* Double-clicks, concurrent requests, delayed webhooks and uncertain responses do not create duplicate charges.
* The actor and provider-confirmed outcome appear in transaction history.
* Sandbox and browser QA cover success, decline, pending, missing recovery URL, stale eligibility and permission denial before release.

## Open questions

Confirm who may retry charges when this backlog work is scheduled. Recommended initial scope is owner/admin, with no automatic customer messages.

## Whop API references

* Retry an existing payment
* Payment fields, including retryable and recovery_url
* Failed-payment events
* Pending-payment events
* Name 22 setup and delivery

## Implementation context

AI context.md records the deferred scope, provider safety considerations and tests to revisit when scheduled.

relatedSnapshot.title: Keep reminding customers while their plan payment is failing
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What we want

When a plan payment fails, the workspace Owners and Admins hear from us straight away and keep hearing from us until it's fixed or the plan ends, instead of getting one notice or none.

## Why

* In production nobody gets our payment-failed warning today. It sits behind the same switch as the campaign pauses and workspace removals, and that switch is off, so Stripe's own email is the only notice.
* After the first notice there is nothing until the plan ends about 14 days later. In the 30 days to 11 September, about 220 plans had a failed payment and most expired without the customer paying.
* We want to turn off Stripe's failed-payment emails and send our own instead.

Follows ENG-13746, whose first part (recording failed payments and the first warning) shipped in PR Acquisity/Acquisity#7195.

## How it should work

### First warning

Sent as soon as a plan payment fails, whether or not the switch is on. Pausing campaigns, cancelling AI SDR follow-ups and removing workspaces still wait for the switch.

### Reminder emails (Autumn plans)

* Day 3 and day 7: "Payment still failing for {workspace}".
* Day 12, about two days before the plan usually ends: "Final reminder: payment still failing for {workspace}".
* Before each one we check with Autumn that the payment is still failing. If the customer has paid or the plan has changed, the reminders stop.

## Decisions already made

* Day 12 stands in for "two days before the end", because the 14-day expiry is what we see in the data, not a fixed rule.
* Reminders cover the plan only, not domains or inboxes, and are email only.
* Whop workspaces get the first warning but not the reminders.

## Not doing

* An update-card or billing link in the emails. That's a separate small follow-up, links for our own workspaces only.
* The Stripe decline reason, the in-app alert and the "Payment failing" label. They stay on ENG-13746's list.

## Done when

- [ ] A workspace whose plan payment fails gets the payment-failed email in production while the switch is still off.
- [ ] A test Autumn customer that stays past due gets the day 3, day 7 and final reminders, once per recipient.
- [ ] A customer who pays before a reminder is due gets no further reminders.
- [ ] Campaigns are not paused and workspaces are not removed while the switch is off.
- [ ] Tests cover the reminder schedule, the stop on payment and a retried send.

<details><summary>For whoever builds it</summary>

* PR: Acquisity/Acquisity#7248
* Job: `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/send-autumn-payment-reminders.ts` (`billing.send-autumn-payment-reminders`)
* Check: `apps/web/lib/billing/autumn-payment-reminders.ts`
* Switch: `SUBSCRIPTION_ACCESS_AUTOMATION_ENABLED`, unset in production
* Docs: `docs/agents/billing.md`
  </details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Payments from payment links mark deals won when "mark paid deals as won" is on
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a closer sends a payment link and the buyer pays, the deal should move to won if the workspace has switched on "Mark eligible deals as won when they are paid". Today it never does for payment-link payments, because Acquisity cannot tell which product they were for.

## Problem

AI Acquisition switched the setting on for its four HT pipelines on 2 Oct 2026, and not one deal has moved since. Every payment link creates its own one-off price plan in Whop. Acquisity only recognises plans it has already synced, so all 305 payment-link payments from 1 Sep to 4 Oct are treated as "product not mapped" and refused. Examples: `pay_06iJyIWLTtP2rL` (2 Oct) and `pay_zUiGapeEQU56s4` (4 Oct) were paid after the switch and neither deal moved.

The same gap leaves some payments with no product and no cash category at all, for example `pay_t6rSsTEwHPOC9w` ($9,000, plan `plan_Aoe6j4T3oXDIf`). Closers' paid deals stay open and Closed is too low.

## How it should work

* When a payment's plan is not synced, work out the product from the payment itself (its synced product) and use that product's enabled configuration.
* Everything else about the setting is unchanged: only successful, non-refunded payments, only in categories that earn closer credit, only in the chosen pipelines, and the payment's own deal is the one that moves.
* Payments under $5 never move a deal to won, so card tests and test purchases cannot win deals (decided by James, 5 Oct 2026). Staff email exclusion is not part of this ticket.
* The product and cash category also show correctly on the payment and in cash reporting.

## Done when

* A payment-link payment for a mapped product, on a deal in a chosen pipeline, moves that deal to won within the normal processing time.
* The auto-win review list no longer shows "Product not mapped" for payment-link payments whose product is mapped.
* A payment on an unsynced plan shows its product and cash category.
* A payment under $5 on an eligible deal leaves the deal where it is.
* The DEAL-1 and CASH-6 checks in Saher's Floor Command acceptance pack return no new rows after release.

## Implementation context

Classification happens in `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/services/payment-auto-win-service.ts` (around lines 185 to 200, `classifyCrmFloorCommandCashMapping`) and the same mapping in `crm-floor-command-cash.ts` (around lines 107 to 109). Both look up `matchedSyncedPlanId`; the payment already carries `syncedProductId`. Alternative if cleaner: sync the plan a payment link creates when the link is made.

relatedSnapshot.title: Filter Smart Views by payment method, refunds, failures, plan terms and buyer details
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps can filter People and Deals by the details of a payment: how it was paid, refunds, failures, disputes, fees and net, currency, the plan it was sold on, who owned it at payment time, and who the buyer said they were at checkout.

## Problem

The CRM stores these details on every payment but only amount, date, status and product can be filtered. "Payments that failed today", "refunded more than $500 this week" and "subscriptions paid by bank" are not possible without opening each payment.

## Proposed fix

Add the remaining per-payment fields to the Smart View filter builder for People and Deals, including plan terms read from the link version the payment was made against.

## What's included

* Payment method used, refund amount, refund date, failure date, failure reason, dispute date, fee amount, net received, payment currency.
* Link creator at payment and deal owner at payment, with the existing closer override applied.
* Buyer name, buyer email, buyer phone.
* Plan terms: schedule type (one-off, subscription, split pay), contract value, annualized value, initial amount, renewal amount, billing interval, required instalment count, trial period and expiry period.
* Existing refunded, partially refunded, failed and disputed status filters stay as they are.

Excludes link engagement fields, totals and same-record matching, which are separate children of ENG-13462.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

* Each condition is answered by any one payment on the record.
* Missing provider data is unknown. A payment with no recorded method, fee, buyer detail or plan does not match a positive condition and does not match a negated one either; it matches only "is unknown" style operators where offered.
* Plan terms come from the link version the payment was made against. Manually recorded payments have none and read as unknown.
* Ownership fields use the values recorded at payment time, never the deal's current owner.
* Buyer email is compared against the contact's canonical email so reps can find a buyer whose checkout email differs from the linked contact.
* Method used is separate from the methods offered on the link.
* Relative dates follow the view's existing timezone rules.

## Who can do what

Same as the existing payment filters from ENG-12239. No raw provider payloads, credentials or full card details are exposed; card brand and last four are not offered as filters.

## What the user sees

The new fields appear in the filter picker under a payments group. Amounts are entered in whole currency units. Select fields list only the values the workspace has. Previews and saved views behave as today.

## Done when

- [ ] Every listed field can be selected, combined, previewed, saved, reopened and shared in People and Deals views.
- [ ] "Payments failed today", "refunded more than $500 this week" and "subscriptions paid by bank" return the correct records.
- [ ] A payment with no recorded method, fee or buyer detail matches neither the positive nor the negated condition.
- [ ] Manual payments read plan terms as unknown.
- [ ] Attribution filters use payment-time ownership and the closer override, not the deal's current owner.
- [ ] Preview count, list, saved execution and sample mode agree for every field and operator.
- [ ] Client-role and cross-workspace requests fail closed.
- [ ] Browser QA and verified activation events cover the changed flow.

## Open questions

* Which contact email buyer-email comparison uses when a contact has several. Recommended default: the canonical contact email only.

## Expected outcome

Payment follow-up on failures, refunds, disputes and plan types is a saved view.

## Implementation context

* This ticket's context: AI context.md.
* Parent context: AI context.md on ENG-13462.
* Schedule type and plan terms are not stored on the payment. They live on the payment link version the payment references, so this ticket adds that join. Manual payments have no version.
* Method, buyer phone, dispute date and link creator at payment are each written from a single place in the provider webhook path, so production coverage should be confirmed before promising negated filters on them.

relatedSnapshot.title: Payment provider disconnect guardrails: warn when live subscriptions / split-pay plans / unpaid links exist
relatedSnapshot.description:
Found in the code review of the ENG-11109 Stripe provider branch. With two providers supported, clients will "switch" processors by disconnecting one — and disconnect currently creates a silent visibility trap.

## Current behavior (verified in code)

1. Disconnect does **not** cancel anything at the provider — Whop memberships and Stripe subscription schedules (`end_behavior: cancel`) keep charging customers on their own. (Correct, disconnect shouldn't nuke client revenue.)
2. But the webhook endpoint is **deleted** on disconnect and the secret cleared (`disconnectCrmPaymentProviderConnection`, `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/services/provider-connections.ts:388-424`) → renewal payments, refunds, and disputes for still-running subscriptions never reach the CRM again.
3. The reconcile and catalog-sync crons filter to `status = Active` only — no backstop for disconnected connections. Customers keep paying; the CRM silently stops seeing it.
4. Unpaid links on the disconnected connection fail closed at checkout ("Payment provider connection is not active", `payment-links.ts:142-149`) — correct, but buyers holding old links hit an error.
5. Recovery requires reconnecting first: historical import asserts an Active connection (`import-provider-payments.ts:44,133-137`). Nothing prompts the user to do this.

## Proposed fix

Before disconnecting a connection, warn (or block) when it still has:

* active subscriptions / split-pay plans (data is in the synced catalog / payment tables), and/or
* unpaid active payment links bound to it.

Show counts in the confirmation dialog. Optionally: an "import remaining history" prompt on reconnect.

## Acceptance

* Disconnect confirmation surfaces live-plan and unpaid-link counts for that connection.
* Docs/help copy explains that in-flight subscriptions keep charging at the provider and stop being tracked after disconnect.

relatedSnapshot.title: Attach payment plans to existing Whop memberships automatically
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What we want

When a rep sends a payment-plan link to a customer who already paid a deposit on the same Whop product, the plan should attach to the buyer's existing Whop membership automatically — no refusal, no manual work in the Whop dashboard.

## Why

PR #7384 (ENG-15670) stops Acquisity creating links Whop will always reject, so reps get a clear error instead of a dead link. But the sale still has to happen: today the rep's only options are a one-time payment or a different product, which loses the agreed instalment schedule. Confirmed in prod for `<email>` on the AIA Name 1 product.

## How it should work

* Rep creates the payment-plan link exactly as before. For a returning buyer the link opens a Whop "save your payment method" page (setup-mode checkout, $0 today) instead of a rejected checkout.
* Once the buyer saves a card, Acquisity attaches the agreed plan to their Whop membership server-side: same deferred first-charge date, same instalment amounts, billing stops when the instalment count completes.
* Name 18 land on the deal like normal Whop payments.
* A buyer who abandons the save page can reopen the link and try again.

## Decisions already made

* Keep the #7384 detection as the trigger for the automatic path, and as the refusal fallback when the automatic path can't run.
* Use Whop's supported primitives only: setup-mode checkout configuration -> `setup_intent.succeeded` webhook -> `POST /payments` with the member's saved payment method and the same renewal/split-pay plan attributes used at checkout.

## Open questions

* Whether `POST /payments` honours `split_pay_required_payments` and `trial_period_days` server-side — verify before merge; use Whop's documented equivalent if not.

## Done when

- [ ] A returning buyer who already paid a deposit can open a payment-plan link, save a card, and end up with an active plan on the agreed schedule.
- [ ] First charge happens on the agreed deferred date, instalments match the quoted amounts, and billing stops after the final instalment.
- [ ] No duplicate memberships or duplicate charges for the returning buyer.
- [ ] A returning buyer who never completes the save step leaves the link payable.
- [ ] Tests cover the setup-intent -> plan-attach flow and the refusal fallback.

<details><summary>For whoever builds it</summary>

* Parent: ENG-15670, PR #7384 (the detect/refuse guard in `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/services/returning-whop-buyer.ts`).
* Checkout builder: `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/providers/whop/checkout.ts` (`mode: 'setup'` variant).
* Name 22 events already subscribed incl. `setup_intent.*`: `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/providers/whop/webhooks.ts`.
* Provider event pipeline: `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/services/provider-events.ts` (setup_intent currently routed to activity only).
* Plan schedule helpers: `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/checkout-schedule.ts` (`getFirstRenewalDelayDays`, `getWhopSplitPaymentCount`).
* Needs a Whop sandbox company/API key for live e2e evidence (none in vault today).
* Pinned SDK `<mention>/<email>` supports checkout setup mode, `setupIntents`, `payments.create`, `paymentMethods.list`.
  </details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Whop catalog sync re-activates archived plans, so the CRM product currency stays on the archived plan
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A CRM Payments product whose old Whop plans were archived keeps showing the archived plan's currency in **Settings → Payments → Products**, and the currency cannot be changed from the UI. Archiving the old plans in Whop, running Sync now, and toggling the product off and on does not move it, because the catalog sync re-activates any plan Whop still returns and the product currency is derived from that plan.

## Problem

In Settings → Payments → Products the Currency column shows CAD for a product whose active Whop plans are all USD. The admin archived the 9 old CAD plans in Whop, synced, and turned the product off and on, and it still shows CAD.

Because payment links inherit the product currency, a link created for that product drafts in CAD and the Whop plan Acquisity creates for the link is CAD too. On a CAD link the USD-only rails (bank transfer, ClarityPay, Name 13) cannot be offered at all, so the wrong currency also costs the workspace those payment methods.

## Root cause

Two things compound.

1. The catalog sync never archives a plan Whop still returns. `planToInsert` in `apps/web/lib/crm-payments/providers/whop/catalog-sync.ts` hardcodes `status: active` for every plan in the response, and `upsertSyncedPlan` in `catalog-upserts.ts` writes `status = excluded.status` on conflict, so a plan Whop reports with `visibility: archived` is re-activated on every sync. The reader (`providers/whop/catalog-reader.ts`) calls `whop.plans.list` with only `account_id`, `company_id`, `first` and `after`, and no `visibilities` filter, although the pinned SDK's `PlanListParams` supports `visibilities` including `not_archived`. The archive sweep in `catalog-sync.ts` only archives plans absent from the response, so it never sees these.
2. The product currency is derived once and then sticks. `crm_payment_product_config.currency` is written by the sync's first-insert path and by `crm.payments.updateProductConfig`, which resolves `currency = defaultPlan?.currency ?? firstPlan?.currency ?? existingConfig?.currency`. The Products row (`components/crm/payments/product-catalog-row.tsx`) displays `config.currency ?? defaultPlan.currency ?? 'usd'` and sends `defaultSyncedPlanId` as the plan the config already points at. While the archived CAD plan is still active here it remains the default plan, so off/on re-derives CAD.

## Evidence (2026-10-13)

* Product "6-Month AI Name 25 Bootcamp" (provider product `<stripe-id>`) holds 609 USD plans (608 hidden, 1 visible) and 9 CAD plans in `crm_payment_synced_plan`. All 9 CAD rows have `visibility = 'archived'` and `status = 'active'`, with `last_synced_at` 2026-10-13T19:50:04Z, so the sync that ran at 19:50 rewrote them as active.
* The product's config row holds `currency = 'cad'` with `default_synced_plan_id` pointing at one of those 9 archived CAD plans (provider plan `plan_kPf1moutBWKAp`); the row was last updated 2026-10-13T19:49:15Z by the off/on.
* Blast radius in production: 45 plan rows are `visibility = 'archived'` with `status = 'active'`, across 8 workspaces and 18 products.
* The catalog sync cron runs daily (`0 3 * * *`), so a one-off data fix on its own would be reverted the following night.

## Suggested fix

* Make the plan read agree with Whop: pass `visibilities: ['not_archived']`, and/or set the stored status from `plan.visibility === 'archived'` in `planToInsert`, so the upsert and the archive sweep cannot disagree.
* Re-derive `crm_payment_product_config.currency` from an active plan when the stored default plan is archived (and clear or repoint `default_synced_plan_id` when it points at an archived plan), so a workspace that has already archived its old plans recovers on the next config save instead of needing an internal data fix.
* Workspaces already in this state need a one-off correction of the plan rows and the product config, otherwise the daily sync keeps restoring the archived plans.

## Acceptance criteria

* A plan Whop reports as archived is stored as archived after a sync and stays archived across later syncs.
* A product whose old-currency plans are archived shows the currency of its active plan in Settings → Payments → Products, and links created for it use that currency.
* Plans Whop stops returning are still archived (the existing sweep behaviour is preserved).

## Reproduction

Workspace `<uuid>`, product `<stripe-id>`, Settings → Payments → Products, then open a payment link draft for that product and check the currency.

Reported from Slack (Settings → Payments → Products, Whop connection). Investigated against the code and production catalog rows.
